title: Toby Hardwick's advice and Hodges on dealing with Duke
summary: Hardwick, his friend since early days, gave advice about the band, Hodges told him to know what to say to Duke, and Toby later recorded Come Sunday and left the business.

story.theme_name: Duke Ellington and his orchestra, as others knew them
story.community_name: Duke Ellington: the band, the man, his men

blocks.x: Well, he just -- he was gone. But Toby -- because Toby was my friend, too, because he was one of the first musicians I met when I first started playing, and he told me. So every time I'd see him, he'd sort of give me advice about the band, you know. He'd say, "Don't let them do this to you, because they'll do this to you.
He should know. And, "Don't let Duke do this to you. Watch him." I remember Johnny Hodges telling me, you know, about the first week in the band. He said,

"Listen, if you go to tell Duke anything, be sure you know what you want to say when you go to him, and say it." You know. Then I found out that was the right thing to do, and Toby, he too would tell me, like I said, what to do and what not to do. And Toby, I remember Toby made some records when he left the band. I remember he recorded -- oh, what is the name of that, from, "Black, Brown and --," "Come Sunday."
I remember he recorded "Come Sunday," and you know, he had record dates. Then he sort of went back to Washington and drifted out of the business.
